name: Hanani
overview: Hanani is a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the son of Immer. His mention in Scripture is connected to a significant family circumstance involving intermarriage with a foreign wife, as recorded in Ezra 10:20. No additional personal details or notes are provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Hanani is a proper name meaning "gracious." This meaning reflects a positive attribute but is not indicated as being given directly by God in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Hanani is explicitly noted as a descendant of Immer, establishing his lineage within the Levitical tribe. Beyond this relationship, Scripture does not record any other family connections for him apart from the fact that his father had married a foreign wife.
scriptureSignificance: Hanani's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his identification as the son of Immer, who had married a foreign wife, highlighting issues of covenant faithfulness and purity among the returning exiles. His mention in Ezra 10:20 situates him within the community's efforts to maintain holiness and obedience to God's commands during the post-exilic period.
